title: Effectuating Overturned Quantity Limit Denials — Utilization Management Program Authorization Reference
content:
When a member's appeal under the Member Appeals Program overturns the denial of a quantity limit exception request on an acute migraine drug — sumatriptan, Ubrelvy or Nurtec ODT — under the Utilization Management Program, the authorization owed for that overturned appeal is put in force for the drug.

## Governing rule

The authorization owed after the overturn carries the quantity per rolling 30 days the Utilization Management Program determines for overturned quantity limit denials. It runs from the overturn date for the package's quantity limit approval months under the general approval-period rule of the program.

## What the effectuation records

One effectuation records one new quantity limit authorization for the drug that came about through the appeal overturn, linked to the opening of the denied case, with the quantity per rolling 30 days it covers and its first and last days in force. The denied case itself keeps its decision. Afterwards the member's authorizations list it.

## How it is invoked

The tool is `grant_overturn_authorization_6da113c2`, an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. The effectuation is complete when the receipt shows status "in_force".

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | the customer reference number of the member, as read from the customer profile lookup | identifier |
| `review_program_id` | the reference number of the member's Utilization Management Program, as read from the review program lookup | identifier |
| `source_case_id` | the reference number of the opening of the denied case the appeal overturned, as named on the appeal and read from the appeal or review case lookup | identifier |
| `drug_name` | the drug the authorization covers | one value of the drug list below |
| `approved_quantity_per_30` | the quantity of the drug per rolling 30 days the authorization covers | decimal units, up to 3 decimals |
| `effective_date` | the first day the authorization is in force | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `expiration_date` | the last day the authorization is in force | YYYY-MM-DD |

**`drug_name` values:** `atorvastatin`, `lisinopril`, `metformin`, `sertraline`, `levothyroxine`, `sumatriptan`, `oxycodone-acetaminophen`, `insulin glargine-yfgn`, `Lantus`, `Eliquis`, `Xarelto`, `Jardiance`, `Ozempic`, `Mounjaro`, `Wegovy`, `Zepbound`, `Trelegy Ellipta`, `Breztri Aerosphere`, `Nurtec ODT`, `Ubrelvy`, `Humira`, `adalimumab-adaz`, `Dupixent`, `Skyrizi`, `Rinvoq`, `Enbrel`, `Biktarvy`, `Ibrance`.

## Receipt

A successful call returns `authorization_id` (the reference number of the new authorization), `drug_name`, `auth_basis` (always `appeal_overturn`), `approved_quantity_per_30` (up to 3 decimals), `effective_date` and `expiration_date` (YYYY-MM-DD) and status "in_force".

*Hypothetical illustration:* an effectuation for `Ubrelvy` with `approved_quantity_per_30` 20 returns an `authorization_id`, `auth_basis` `appeal_overturn` and status "in_force"; the denied case still shows its denial.
